label: Projector Screens
title: The Shape of Everything, 2026
oneLiner: Sound and image, one whole world.
body:
Jteve Sobs
The Shape of Everything, 2026

Jteve Sobs works across sound and
moving image, treating them as one
medium. Using layers of generative ai,
the work centers on speculative
worldbuilding, including post-human
futures, machine consciousness, and
architectures that evoke a beatific vision
of the near future. Each piece is
composed as a complete audiovisual
environment, with sound and image
conceived together from the outset.
highlights: Sound and image, one whole world.
guideLines: Sound and image, one whole world.

label: led camera screens
title: Self Portrait, 2026
body:
Joshua Wolk
Self Portrait, 2026

In a row of digital gilded frames, a
camera studies the face of whoever
stands before it. It searches centuries of
portraiture from the Met, the Art Institute
of Chicago and the Cleveland Museum
of Art for a matching pose and
expression, then lays the painted face
over the living one. For a moment, each
viewer becomes the subject.

label: TVS
title: Mandala, 2026
oneLiner: Make art. Leave a hash. Begin again.
body:
Kevin Esherick
Mandala, 2026

An agent on a sandboxed virtual
machine is instructed to turn the
sandbox itself into a work of art,
continually expanding and improving on
its creation. Every 24 hours, the
machine is wiped. Only a hash of the
previous state is left behind, serving as
the seed for the next. Each day the
agent begins anew.
highlights: Make art. Leave a hash. Begin again.
guideLines: Make art. Leave a hash. Begin again.

label: CPU TERMINALS
body:
COMPUTER

Morry Kolman
Persistence 2, 2026

Persistence 2 is a duet performance where two
computers with extremely limited networking
capabilities attempt to establish a means of
communicating with each other. Kept separate
by a hard firewall, banned from any wireless
connectivity, and without access to common
means of emitting and receiving information
such as microphones, cameras, speakers, and
screens, viewers can watch as these
computers turn to the only means of outreach
they have left: their (quite literal) own devices.
Leveraging agent skills loaded with data
smuggling and airgap jumping techniques from
state of the art security research, the
computers attempt to turn adversarial
exfiltration and hacking methods into a new
means of connection. They must emit and they
must listen; they must take the arbitrary noise
around them as potential signal, while also
understanding how their own lossy
communication may be interpreted by their
counterpart; they grow new senses so that
they may speak a new language.

@WTTDOTM
